title: Patient Experience Across Dental Implant Drilling Protocols
official: Comparative Analysis of Patient Experience Among Under-drilling and Conventional Drilling in Dental Implants: a Randomized Double-blinded Study.
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether the drilling technique used to prepare the implant site affects the experience and satisfaction of adult patients receiving dental implants. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do patients treated with under-drilling report a different experience, satisfaction and postoperative discomfort than patients treated with conventional drilling?
* How are implant insertion torque, implant stability and bone density related to the pain and experience reported by patients?

Researchers will compare under-drilling (the implant site is prepared with a slightly narrower final drill than usual) with conventional drilling (the standard drilling sequence for the implant diameter). Both are standard clinical techniques.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of the two techniques, without knowing which one they receive
* Have their dental implant(s) placed at the CEU Cardenal Herrera University Dental Clinic
* Complete a questionnaire about their experience before surgery and immediately after surgery
* Record their experience every day during the first week after surgery
* Complete a quality-of-life questionnaire (OHIP-14) one week after surgery
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older
* Partially or completely edentulous patients requiring dental implant placement
* Signed informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Use of psychotropic or pain-modulating medication
* Systemic conditions affecting bone healing
* Use of medication known to interfere with bone metabolism
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding
* Allergy or intolerance to implant materials (e.g., titanium, zirconia)
* Severe bruxism or severe temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders
* Inability to follow postoperative care protocols or maintain basic oral hygiene
* Psychological or cognitive impairment that may interfere with understanding or following postoperative care instructions
* Inability to attend follow-up visits
* Previous implant failure
